The only company bar is qualitative: H2 2026 revenue above H1 (H1 = $3.4m + $3.25m = $6.65m) and lower H2 opex from $4m of annualised cuts (Q2 call 2026-07-29: https://www.webull.com/news/15364343962084352). first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is tiny and stale. 70.0k shares short with 1.9 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement, about 0.3% of 21.8m shares (search snippet citing https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/awre/short-interest/, page 403; Equibles has about 0.16% of float: https://equibles.com/stocks/awre/shortinterest). Not a crowded short. No usable option chain: total OI 12 and ATM not two-sided, so skew and implied move are null (sealed baseline). evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-07-29) management said H2 2026 revenue will exceed H1 ($6.65m) and H2 opex will be lower as $4m of annualised cuts (started Q2) take full effect. So Q3 operating loss should narrow from Q2's $2.7m, and a Q3 near or above $3.3m sits inside the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 2026, with H2 > H1 guided, the stock rose +3.6%, the only up reaction in 7 prints (baseline). Q3 2025 revenue +33% still fell -5.95%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own guide and lands inside it. The stock fell from about $1.25 in August to $0.90 with no news, so the market is not paying for a second-half recovery. If it were, the stock would not sit about 20% below its post-Q2 level and near cash.
evidence.independence: Same guide restated in biometricupdate's 2026-07-30 coverage (https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/aware-focussed-on-public-sector-opportunity-for-biometrics-orchestration-platform). Same source event, so one finding.

evidence.text: Q3 2025 revenue was $5.1m (+33% YoY), including a one-time $1m perpetual-licence expansion with an existing customer and $0.6m of new term licences. Unless a large licence lands, Q3 2026 revenue will be headlined as a YoY decline. Q1 and Q2 2026 were down 6% and 16%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: YoY revenue declines in Q4 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 drew -6.55%, -20.55% and +3.6% (baseline; Q1 reaction per Zacks 'Aware Stock Dips Post Q1 Earnings, Revenue Declines Y/Y', https://www.metatrader.com/fr/news/1578611-aware-stock-dips-post-q1-earnings-revenue-declines-yy).
evidence.why_not_priced: The comparison is mechanical and public, but this name's thin base trades on the Zacks/wire YoY headline. If the market had priced a clean sequential read, the last three YoY-decline headlines would not have drawn mostly negative reactions.
evidence.independence: Q2 2026 10-Q shows software licences falling to $954k from $1,420k YoY (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1015739/000119312526328344/awre-20260630.htm). This is a different document confirming licence softness.

evidence.text: Current deferred revenue was $3.462m at 2026-06-30, against $3.911m at 2025-06-30 (-11.5% YoY) and $4.025m at 2024-06-30. It is the lowest June level in the series. Q2 maintenance revenue fell 7% YoY ($1,998k vs $2,148k). The recurring base going into the Q3 renewal season is shrinking.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction is attributable to deferred revenue specifically. Recurring-revenue softness was cited alongside the -20.55% Q1 2026 reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: The figure has been in the 10-Q since 2026-07-31, but no coverage read the YoY deferred-revenue walk. Coverage summarised recurring revenue as 'roughly flat at $2.7m'. If it had been priced, the post-Q2 reaction would not have been the only up move in seven prints.
evidence.independence: Q2 10-Q revenue table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1015739/000119312526328344/awre-20260630.htm). Same filing family as finding 2's corroboration but a different line (maintenance vs licences).

evidence.text: The CEO (Ajay Amlani) made open-market purchases between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-12, about 26.6k shares at $1.18-1.26 (Form 4s filed 2026-08-04, 08-07, 08-12). They were made after the Q2 print with knowledge of July and August trading, and he is now underwater at $0.90.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider-buy-to-print reaction found.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and small (about $33k). The stock has fallen about 28% since, so the signal has not supported the price. That is weak evidence it is priced or uninformative.
evidence.independence: Further purchases on 2026-08-05/06 and 08-11/12 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1015739/000119312526340202/ownership.xml, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1015739/000119312526347341/ownership.xml) are the same insider, so one finding.

evidence.text: Market cap is about $19.6m (21.81m shares x $0.8964). Cash and securities were $16.84m at 2026-06-30, with no debt and H1 operating cash burn of $5.44m. Estimated September 30 cash is about $14m, so the operating business is valued at roughly $5m at about 0.4x sales.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. The same cash-backed setup existed before the -20.55% Q1 reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Cheapness is visible to anyone, so it is not an edge. It only bounds the downside on a bad print. Zacks already flagged EV/Sales of about 0.4x in April and rated it Underperform (https://www.metatrader.com/it/news/1508545-awre-downgraded-to-underperform-on-delayed-conversions--cash).
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: The stock closed at $0.8405 on 2026-10-15 and $0.8964 on 2026-10-28, below Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum bid. EDGAR shows no deficiency-notice 8-K through the last filing on 2026-09-24. The release or call could disclose a notice or reverse-split plans.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance for this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The price is public, but a 30-business-day breach has probably not run yet, so no notice exists to price. The date the stock first closed below $1 is unverified, so this may resolve after the window.
evidence.independence: Yahoo close of $0.8405 on 2026-10-15 (snippet, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AWRE/chart/).

evidence.text: The DHS-only funding lapse ran from 2026-02-14 to about 2026-04-30. On the Q2 call the CEO cited DHS funding disruption and said public-sector business development was up. Q3 contains the federal fiscal year-end (September), and a CR averted any lapse at the start of FY2027 (signed early September). Federal licence timing therefore had a clean window in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Federal procurement delays were cited for the Q2 decline. No reaction is attributable to a federal win.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. No Aware federal award was announced from August to October, which argues it has not converted. The size is small for that reason.

first_hunter_context.bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $231-235m, adjusted EBITDA $32-34m, non-GAAP EPS $0.45-0.49; FY2026 revenue $900-910m, adj. EBITDA $123-125m, non-GAAP EPS $1.71-1.79 (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000055/q220268kexh991.htm, 2026-07-29). FY cloud communications guide $622-626m from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808). Sell-side Q3 revenue consensus was not found from two agreeing sources. Pre-guide consensus was $223.6m / $0.40 (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bandwidth-q2-earnings-top-estimates-strong-ai-driven-demand), and Benzinga still shows $0.40 EPS. So the bar is the company guide, with $233m / $0.47 at the midpoint. Implied Q4 revenue is about $238-248m (FY guide less Q1 $208.8m, Q2 $219.9m and a Q3 midpoint of $233m).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is 5,117,810 shares, 16.79% of float, 7.0 days to cover, as of the 2026-10-15 record date (FINRA, published 2026-10-26). That is up 8.4% from 4,723,069 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BAND/short-interest/). In March 2026 it was about 1.17m shares and 2.3 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/band/shortinterest), so the short has roughly quadrupled. Sealed baseline: skew_25d +4.16 vol points (downside paid, moderate), put/call open-interest ratio 0.36 (call-heavy), ATM spread 36% of mid. Tape: spot $50, 20d -17.6%, 5d +6.8%, 36% below the 52-week high, 290% above the 52-week low, 20d realised vol 99%. This is a crowded and rising short into a print on a name that has moved +52% and -29% on its last two releases.

evidence.text: Short interest rose 8.4% in the last fortnight to 5.12m shares, 16.8% of float and 7.0 days to cover (2026-10-15 record date, published 2026-10-26), about 4x the ~1.17m of March 2026. The build came into a 17.6% 20-day drawdown, including an unexplained -8.8% on 2026-10-08 and a thin-volume -14.3% intraday print on 2026-10-22. Against that, call open interest is about 3x put open interest (P/C 0.36).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows +52.1% on 2026-04-30, when a Q1 beat over the top of the guide met a de-rated stock, and -29.3% on 2026-07-29, when a beat met a stock that had run up 277% over twelve months. Short interest at those dates is not on file, but the March 2026 reading was 1.17m shares.
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest is a public number. The point is that the short is near its high exactly when the stock has given back 36% from its high, so the downside case is already partly in the price and in the short. If the market expected a squeeze, the 20-day trend would not be -17.6% and the skew would not be put-paid. The +6.8% five-day bounce may be early covering.
evidence.independence: Drawdown evidence: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-bandwidth-nasdaq-band-stock-falls-88-whats-next-2026-10-08/ and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-bandwidth-nasdaq-band-stock-price-down-143-heres-why-2026-10-22/ (no cause given; the 10-22 move was on volume about 90% below average). Call-heavy open interest comes from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options), a different source from FINRA.

evidence.text: Q3 revenue is likely at or above the $235m top of the guide, but mostly through pass-through surcharges. Bandwidth beat its own guide in Q1 (actual $208.8m against $200-203m) and landed at the top in Q2 ($219.9m against $214-220m). Q3 is the first quarter carrying full-period carrier surcharge increases: AT&T 10DLC SMS $0.0030 to $0.0035 and MMS $0.0075 to $0.0090 from 2026-04-01, and T-Mobile 10DLC $0.003 to $0.004 from 2026-01-19. Surcharge revenue already rose from about $59m in Q1 to $68m in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue at the top of the guide, partly from surcharges, and the stock fell 29.3% because the beat was read as pass-through and low quality (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-7-29-why-bandwidth-band-stock-is-nosediving). Q1 2026: a 2.9% beat over the top of the guide, and the stock rose 52.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management knew the surcharge schedule when it guided on 2026-07-29, so most of this sits inside the $231-235m guide. Any upside is a beat on total revenue, not on cloud communications, and that is the line the market discounts. If the market priced a quality beat, there would be no 17% drawdown into the print.
evidence.independence: T-Mobile fee change: https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/44609260499995-T-Mobile-Messaging-Carrier-Fee-Changes-January-2026. Guide-beat record: the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000014/q420258kexh991.htm) and the Q2 release. All are primary documents.

evidence.text: The line that sank Q2 is gross margin quality. GAAP gross margin fell to 36% from 40% on surcharges, and FY non-GAAP EPS was trimmed to $1.71-1.79 from $1.77-1.83 for infrastructure investment. Morgan Stanley's initiation (2026-10-16, Equal-weight, $56 target) puts gross profit on incremental cloud revenue at about 68% in Q2 2026, against 82% in FY2025. Management guided non-GAAP gross margin up in Q3-Q4 to about 60% for the year (Q2: 59.4%), and its Q3 EPS guide of $0.45-0.49 implies a step-up from Q2's $0.37.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-29: gross margin down 4.1 points year on year and the FY EPS trim drove a -29.3% day despite a raised revenue guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: The concern is in the wire, so it is partly priced. What is not priced is the sign of the Q3 incremental margin: management committed to expansion, while MS shows the incremental trend going the other way. A print that confirms ~60% would remove the bear case, and one below 59% would repeat Q2. Net sign is slightly negative because the name has punished margin quality before.
evidence.independence: Primary: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000055/q220268kexh991.htm), GAAP 36% against 40% and non-GAAP 59% against 58%. Management's ~60% FY target is from the call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808). Two documents, one concern.

evidence.text: Guidance setup. The FY cloud communications guide of $622-626m (about 11% growth) explicitly 'left out ... any future benefit related to Salesforce', and management said 'there's some conservatism in our model' (Q2 call, 2026-07-29). On 2026-09-15, after that guide, Bandwidth announced it is the first certified carrier for the global rollout of Salesforce's native Contact Center across 25+ countries 'this fall', via BYOC on Maestro. The same day it filed an investor deck (8-K 7.01) reiterating '20% revenue growth and 33% Adjusted EBITDA growth for 2026'. The FY revenue guide has been raised twice ($864-884m to $880-900m to $900-910m). Implied Q4 is about $238-248m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raised FY guides: +52.1% in April 2026 (raise with a beat) and -29.3% in July 2026 (revenue raised, EPS trimmed, H2 cloud deceleration flagged). The guide is the line this stock trades on, in both directions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Salesforce expansion was announced and the stock still fell from about $61 at end-September to $50, so the market is not paying for a raise. The guide excludes Salesforce by management's own statement. If a raise were priced, the 20-day trend and the put-paid skew would look different. Morgan Stanley's EW and BofA's Neutral show the sell-side is not underwriting upside either.
evidence.independence: Salesforce release: https://finviz.com/news/392175/bandwidth-and-salesforce-expand-collaboration-to-support-the-global-rollout-of-salesforces-native-contact-center. Guide exclusion and 'conservatism' quotes: https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808 (separate document). Piper Sandler estimates the voice-only Agentforce opportunity at +2-3 points of growth in 2027-28 (via the MS article).

evidence.text: Peer read after Bandwidth last spoke: Twilio's Q2 release on 2026-08-06 raised its FY2026 organic growth guide to 13-13.5% from 9.5-10.5%, with dollar-based net expansion of 116% (108% a year earlier). That points to strong CPaaS and voice/agent demand through mid-2026.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history on peer read-throughs for this name. Bandwidth's own commercial net retention rose to 113% (+3 points q/q) in Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public, has been available for 12 weeks and was surely seen. It is filed because it postdates Bandwidth's guide and supports a cloud-revenue beat. Bandwidth's 17% 20-day decline suggests the market is not extrapolating it.
evidence.independence: Proxy only. Twilio is a competitor, not a counterparty, and its Q3 2026 print had not been released as of 2026-10-28.

evidence.text: Political messaging: FY2026 political revenue was cut to $13m from $15m, with about $1m in Q2 and the rest 'principally in the second half'. Local reports through mid-October describe surging midterm texting (e.g. Alaska on 2026-10-15; Oklahoma at '10,000 texts per hour' in July). No 2026 volume count was found.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Political revenue was $46m in the twelve months to June 2025 and $3m in the twelve months to June 2026 (investor deck slide 9). No resolved reaction history isolates this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company lowered the political number, so the bar is conservative. At $13m on a ~$905m year the line is small, and even a 50% overshoot is about $6m, roughly 1% of H2 revenue.
evidence.independence: Proxy, anecdotal: https://www.fox13news.com/news/political-texts-surging-2026-here-how-reduce. The $13m comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808).

evidence.text: Capital return capacity. The credit agreement's third amendment (effective 2026-07-25) doubled the annual restricted-payment cap to $40m (or 20% of TTM EBITDA). About $60m of the $80m buyback authorization remained at 2026-06-30. In August the company repurchased $20.8m principal of its 2028 converts at a discount, leaving only $6.7m outstanding. The Q3 print will disclose any buyback at depressed prices.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction. The $80m program was announced with the Q4 2025 print (+11.9% day, alongside other news).
evidence.why_not_priced: The covenant change sits in an 8-K item 1.01 that no preview mentions. The Q3 buyback amount is unknown until the release. Size is small because $40m a year is about 2.5% of a ~$1.5bn market cap.
evidence.independence: Convert repurchase 8-K 8.01: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000060/0001514416-26-000060.txt (separate document). Remaining authorization per the Q2 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001514416/000151441626000057/band-20260630.htm.

evidence.text: Director Lukas Roush sold 1,500 shares at $49.04 on 2026-10-16 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-05-28. His Form 144 covers 4,500 shares and he holds 58,769 after the sale. An insider Form 144 cluster on 2026-08-27 was followed by Form 4s on 2026-09-01 to 09-03.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None.
evidence.why_not_priced: The plan was pre-scheduled and the sale is tiny. It carries almost no information, which is why it is sized near zero.
evidence.independence: EDGAR filing list: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001514416&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

evidence.text: The $13m of 2026 political revenue does not recur in 2027 (flagged in Morgan Stanley's 2026-10-16 initiation). This is a headwind to the 2027 cloud growth rate, and the formal 2027 guide normally comes with the Q4 print in February.
